hypotheses.reasoning: The origin is a row lock held on notifications by a long-running, idle transaction from template-svc-reconciler (#1141: TRANSACTION 93036 ACTIVE 82 sec, holding 1 lock, undo log entries 1). It was never committed or released, so it sat for over 80 seconds. Template-svc UPDATEs queued behind it and failed with lock wait timeout at notif-db (#1237, #1255), then with statement_timeout inside template-svc (#1267, #1310). Notification-svc then hit ReadTimeout (15s) calling template-svc (#1270), and the gateway returned 504s on POST /v1/notify. The 504s are downstream of this. The logs show the holder but not why the reconciler stalled, so that part is unconfirmed. Ruled out: metrics-agent queue drops (#347) and the TLS expiry warning (#470) are unrelated, and billing-reconciler reports 0 discrepancies throughout.

Alternative reading: the reconciler left the transaction open because a pool or resource in template-svc was exhausted. No pool-exhaustion or OOM logs were found; template-svc GC pauses stayed under 25ms with heap under 46%, so this is weakly supported.

verdict.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck transaction 93036 on notif-db (or restart template-svc-reconciler) to release the notifications row lock, then confirm template-svc UPDATEs succeed and the gateway 504 rate drops. Fix the reconciler so it commits or rolls back promptly and holds locks only briefly, and add an idle-in-transaction timeout on notif-db. Find the reconciler code path that opened the transaction and stopped before commit.
